follow_ups.ref: The same lens applied to READ_ERRORS and the rest of local/tabs.py -- no second escape found
follow_ups.reason: Enumerated as a class rather than by example. (1) Read path, READ_ERRORS = (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) around export_board.spec_tabs: twelve pathological project-document shapes were driven through tabs.build (empty spec, NUL bytes, malformed and single-column tables, 5000-deep list nesting, a 100 KB heading, a 20 KB bold span, CRLF plus BOM, frontmatter with a non-numeric revision, degenerate PBI and goal markers). All twelve degraded gracefully -- four spec tabs built, one confined warning -- and nothing outside READ_ERRORS escaped. (2) Git path: the residual is derive.git_doc three-way unpack of a log line split on the pipe, a ValueError GIT_ERRORS would not catch. Probed for reachability on a real repository: git folds a multi-line subject into one line for the subject placeholder (a two-line subject prints as one line joined by a space), so every log line carries exactly two pipes and the unpack cannot raise from git own output. It is also shared verbatim with export_board.git_tab, so the two sides cannot diverge. Not raised as a finding on either count. (3) is_repo, git_default, carry, owns, project_of and statuses are pure or total over their inputs.

follow_ups.reason: Re-run on the tree as it now stands, at two strengths. On the real-repository conformance fixture (HAS_GIT true, alpha carrying an origin on github.com so the exporter genuinely would call gh), a full collector pass with the real subprocess.run wrapped by the reviewer recorder made 12 subprocesses, every argv[0] equal to git, none of gh, curl, claude, wget or ssh, and no pulls key on either stored git tab. follow_ups.ref: An OSError on a project data file fails the whole pass, which spec 4.2.1 row 4 does not state -- documentation, not a defect
follow_ups.reason: load_data catches FileNotFoundError (returns an empty dict) and ValueError (re-raised with context), but a PermissionError or other OSError reading the projects data file propagates from outside the confined block and fails the pass, every 60 seconds, until fixed. Row 4 names only ValueError. Deliberately not raised as a finding: it is the same trade the row makes for the same stated reason -- the file holds the hand-kept build state, and treating it as absent would silently reset every PBI of that project to not-started -- and export_board behaves identically, since its main catches only ValueError too. Suggest widening the row 4 wording to any failure to read the data file other than its absence, at the next spec touch.
